commitResults.messageTitle: Update DG NFRs and glossary for TutorContacts
commitResults.messageBody:
The Developer Guide still lists AB3's generic non-functional
requirements and glossary, which do not describe TutorContacts or
the course constraints that apply to it.

Let's replace them with TutorContacts-specific entries:

* Group the NFRs by platform, performance, usability, data and
  reliability, and scope and privacy, drawing on the course
  constraints and the team's MVP specification.
* Make each NFR measurable so that it can be verified.
* Define the domain and UI terms used in the user stories and use
  cases, and drop the unused AB3 term "Private contact detail".

"Normalized name" follows the current implementation: names are
trimmed and compared exactly (case-sensitive).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Add view command for displayed contacts
commitResults.messageBody:
The MVP specification includes a view command, but TutorContacts
has no way to select one contact from the displayed list.

Let's add `view INDEX`, which looks up the contact in the displayed
list and reports `Showing contact: NAME.`, with the error messages
given in the specification. The command is read-only, so it
overrides `isDataChanging()` to avoid rewriting the data file.

Index parsing mirrors DeleteCommandParser so that both commands
accept the same indexes; extracting a shared parser is left as a
follow-up to avoid conflicts with the delete command's owner.

Showing the expanded contact card is deferred to v1.3.

commitResults.messageTitle: Rotate team roles so every member codes each iteration

In v1.2 and v1.3, one member each iteration merged no functional
code, and members kept working in the same component. This limits
everyone's learning and individual code contribution.

Let's make every member a developer who builds features across all
components in every iteration, and rotate the quality and process
duties each iteration. Joel remains team lead for continuity.

commitResults.messageTitle: Enable assertions when running the app with Gradle
commitResults.messageBody:
Java disables assertions by default, so `gradlew run` silently skips
every assert statement and hides broken assumptions during manual
testing.

Let's enable assertions for the Gradle run task and document how to
add `-ea` to the IntelliJ run configuration.

Tests already run with assertions enabled under Gradle, so only the
run task and IDE configuration need changing. The released JAR is
unaffected, so end users never see assertion failures.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Honor equality contracts for contact filters
commitResults.messageBody:
Filter commands and criteria compare their values in equals but inherit
identity-based hash codes. Equal instances can therefore be missed or
stored twice in hash-based collections.

Hash criteria using the same fields as equals and delegate command
hashing to its predicate. Add regression tests that verify equal hashes,
lookup, and duplicate rejection for independently constructed instances.

Both tests reproduce the defects before the fix. All 415 tests, including
UI tests, and both Checkstyle tasks pass on Java 25 after the fix.

Address the two equality-contract review comments on PR #83.
